event.title: Make a Connection!
event.description:
We invite you to spark something new — whether it’s a friendship, a flirtation, or just a fun night out. Join us for Make a Connection!, an evening inspired by the exhibition Hugo McCloud: to everything there is a season.

This event brings people together to discover unexpected common ground. Come ready to mix, mingle, and maybe meet someone who brings a little extra color to your canvas.

What to Expect

  • Cash bar and complimentary light fare beginning at 6:00 pm
  • Quickfire presentations from 6:30–7:15 pm, where participants (or their loyal friends) take the mic for a 2 minute slideshow-style spotlight celebrating their best qualities (attendees can watch without participating)
  • Post-presentation mingling throughout the museum’s galleries, where the connections continue

Presentations

Feeling bold? Want to show off a friend or yourself? Promote yourself or your friends in a positive light with a 2 minute slideshow highlighting best features!

Don’t have someone to present for you? Don’t worry—submit a slideshow and we’ll present it for you.

  1. You must sign up in advance to reserve a spot as space is limited. Fill out our online form by Thursday, November 12, at 8:00 pm.
  2. Keep it fun, friendly, and positive.
  3. Feel free to include images, but make sure that they are appropriate (we have nudes in the museum – we don’t need to see yours).
  4. Keep it short and sweet—each presentation gets 2 minutes! See an example presentation.

MAG reserves the right to review all presentations prior to the event.

For questions about this event, please contact MAG Marketing & Engagement at jgasbarre@mag.rochester.edu. Registration ends on Thursday, November 19, at 6:00 pm. Ticket includes this program and museum admission. Member price is applied through a discount at checkout.

To submit a request for ASL interpretation, please email access@mag.rochester.edu at least two weeks before the event.

event.title: Mindful MAGiC: Sonic Yoga
event.description:
Begin your morning with a restorative experience that blends mindful movement and immersive sound for a powerful journey inward. Set in the serene surroundings of the Fountain Court, this special session features yoga and meditation led by Shanna Pagan and is accompanied by an immersive live soundscape from Harold Taddy (The Gong Situation).

What You Can Bring

  • Yoga mat, bolsters, and layers for comfort
  • Cozy socks
  • A water bottle with a secure, leak-proof lid (no straws)

Important Arrival Details

  • Doors open at 9:00 am
  • Check-in at the Admissions Desk no later than 9:15 am to get situated
  • Please arrive on time to preserve the tranquil nature of the session

The session lasts 9:30–10:30 am, followed by a 15-minute courtesy window to ease your transition into the day. Museum admission begins at 11:00 am when the galleries open to the public.

Come curious. Move with intention. Let the sound guide you.

For questions about this program, contact Katie Nguyen, Senior Manager of Guest Services, at knguyen@mag.rochester.edu.

Ticket sales end on Saturday, November 28, at 9:00 am. Ticket includes museum admission. Member discount applies to the first two tickets in your order.

Students can sign up for as few or as many sessions as they want. Any work made during this time will be bisque for the next session.

Materials

Students will need to purchase clay for their own use. Clay in various varieties is available for purchase at the Creative Workshop for $18.00 per 25lb bag. Glazes and firing are included in the class price. Please bring an old kitchen-sized towel you don’t mind getting dirty.

Registration Information

Registration for this program starts on Tuesday, August 18, at 10:00 am for MAG Members, and Tuesday, August 25, at 10:00 am for Not-Yet-Members. Online registration ends on Monday, December 7, at 3:30 am.

Programs with inadequate enrollment are canceled one week before the first meeting. We will attempt to contact you via email to find an alternative program or to refund your registration fee.

Learn more about classes in the Creative Workshop, including information about parking and the refund and cancellation policies.

event.description:
Make something new at the Memorial Art Gallery! Create art with the Creative Workshop, drop-in for Story Time, follow a guided tour with a Museum Educator, and browse books and toys with the Charlotte Whitney Allen Library.

Free for all ages; no museum ticket required.

Schedule of activities:

  • 10:00 am–1:00 pm: Art-making projects for ages 3 and up. Last projects begin at 12:45 pm.
  • 10:15 am–10:45 am: Story Time.
  • 11:00 am & 12:00 pm: Half-hour, family-friendly tours with a Museum Educator. Sign-up for tours upon arrival.

For questions about this program, email the Creative Workshop at creativeworkshop@mag.rochester.edu.

StART with a Story is sponsored by the Rochester Area Community Foundation.

event.title: Third Thursday Concert—Musical Reflections on MAG’s Medieval Collection
event.description:
leiken, voice & Doug Balliett, organ

On the third Thursday of each month, from October through May, the Eastman School of Music and the Memorial Art Gallery present varied concert programs by faculty and guest artists featuring Eastman’s Italian Baroque Organ. These Third Thursday Concerts are included with museum admission after 5:00 pm and are made possible by the Rippey Endowed Trust.

All concerts begin at 7:00 pm. Please arrive early, as seating is limited and available on a first-come basis.

event.title: Rodrigo Teaser: Michael Lives Forever
event.description:
Step back into the golden era of pop music as Rodrigo Teaser brings the electrifying legacy of Michael Jackson to life in a one-night-only spectacular at Syracuse’s iconic Landmark Theatre.
This isn’t just a concert — it’s a full sensory journey through the career of the King of Pop. From the soulful energy of the Jackson 5 era to the record-shattering anthems of Thriller, Bad, and Dangerous, Rodrigo Teaser channels the voice, the movement, and the unmistakable charisma that made Michael Jackson a global icon. Every glide, spin, and gravity-defying lean is meticulously recreated, transporting the audience straight back to the sold-out arenas and legendary performances that defined a generation.
Backed by a dynamic live band and stunning visual production, the show promises an immersive experience featuring:
Iconic Choreography – Witness the moonwalk, the signature spins, and the sharp, explosive dance breaks that revolutionized pop performance.
Note-Perfect Vocals – From falsetto highs to soulful ballads, the tribute captures the emotional depth and vocal range that made MJ’s music timeless.
Career-Spanning Setlist – Expect beloved favorites and deep-cut gems spanning decades of hits, giving longtime fans and newcomers alike plenty to sing along to.
Dazzling Costumes & Stage Design – Authentic outfit recreations and lighting design pay tribute to the visual artistry that made Jackson’s performances legendary.
Set inside the opulent, historic Landmark Theatre — with its ornate architecture and rich entertainment history — the venue itself adds a layer of grandeur to the evening, making it feel less like a tribute show and more like a genuine trip back in time.
Whether you’re a lifelong Michael Jackson fan who danced to these songs the first time around, or a newer listener discovering the magic for the first time, this show is designed to unite audiences in celebration of one of the most influential artists in music history.

event.title: Bert Kreischer: Permission to Party World Tour
event.description:
Bert Kreischer’s career has evolved from Rolling Stone’s infamous “Number One Partier in the Nation” to one of the top-grossing stand-up comedians in the world—and a powerhouse entrepreneur, actor, producer, content creator, and entertainment brand. Named by Forbes as “one of the best storytellers of his generation,” Kreischer has parlayed his signature comedy and authenticity into a dynamic media empire.

His sixth Netflix special, Lucky, filmed in his hometown of Tampa, FL, sold out all six shows within 24 hours of the on-sale and premiered in Netflix’s Top 10 Most Watched TV Shows in March 2025.

Through Berty Boy Productions, Kreischer oversees hit podcasts and series including Bertcast, Something’s Burning, and 2 Bears, 1 Cave (with Tom Segura), commanding over 16 million fans and 4 billion impressions. He also founded the Fully Loaded Comedy Festival, a touring juggernaut that’s expanded to stadiums, arenas, and sold-out cruises.

In 2024, Kreischer and Segura launched Por Osos Vodka, an award-winning, rapidly expanding spirits brand. Kreischer also starred in and produced Sony Pictures’ The Machine—a feature film adaptation of his legendary stand-up story—which broke into Netflix’s Global Top 10 Films upon release in 2023. His Netflix scripted comedy series Free Bert debuted in January 2026, and quickly broke into Netflix’s U.S. and global Top 10. The show drew millions of viewers in its first weeks, ranking among the platform’s most-watched series worldwide.

event.title: Dr. Neil deGrasse Tyson – Cosmic Collisions
event.description: All the things that go bump in the night (and in the day). And yes, the universe wants to kill you: On occasion these collisions — asteroid & comet impacts on Earth, render life extinct. Learn why and how this happens, and what we are doing (or not doing) about it.

event.title: Theresa Caputo Live! – The Experience
event.description:
For more than a decade, Theresa Caputo—known worldwide as the Long Island Medium—has touched the lives of millions of fans, comforting supporters when they need it most.

Through personal life stories, candid humor, and intimate details about her gift to communicate with those who have passed on, the beloved television personality and best-selling author delivers healing messages to her audience, reassuring them with the revelation that their deceased loved ones are still with them—just in a different way.

Recognized as one of the most renowned mediums for over 20 years, Theresa Caputo Live: The Experience is the awe-inspiring event you won’t want to miss.

event.title: Hell’s Kitchen
event.description:
Contains some strong language and moments with mature themes.

Welcome to HELL’S KITCHEN, the hit musical from 17-time Grammy® Award winning Alicia Keys—inspired by her life, her music, and her community.

Your journey begins with Ali, a 17-year-old girl full of fire, searching for freedom, passion, and her place in the world. Along the way, you’ll meet the musical mentor who changes her life, her dynamic family, and the neighborhood that helps her grow. Relatable, raw, and refreshingly fun, HELL’S KITCHEN is a celebration of finding yourself, your purpose, and the people who lift you up.

More than watching a performance, this experience pulls you out of your seat and has you buzzing when you leave, wondering who to tell about it first. The music—a mix of Keys’ greatest hits and new songs written exclusively for the show—is brought to life through exhilarating choreography. It’s a soundtrack of rebellion, life, and love that speaks to you no matter where you’re from, where you’ve been, or where you’re going.

Hailed as a New York Times Critic’s Pick that is, “thrilling from beginning to end – a rare must-see!” HELL’S KITCHEN is directed by four-time Tony Award nominee Michael Greif (Rent, Dear Evan Hansen and The Notebook), with choreography by four-time Tony Award nominee Camille A. Brown, a book by Pulitzer Prize finalist Kristoffer Diaz, and the music of Alicia Keys.

Feel the energy of this multi-award-winning musical and experience where dreams begin: HELL’S KITCHEN

event.title: New York State Craft Brewers Festival
event.description:
The 13th annual New York State Craft Brewers Festival returns to the historic Landmark Theatre in downtown Syracuse on Saturday, November 21st, 2026. The renowned event brings together 45+ breweries from every region of the state offering enthusiasts, both novice and seasoned, a rare opportunity to relish in unique and award-winning beer. Discover new styles, flavors, and brands, and meet the masters behind the craft you love! Brewery owners & representatives pour at the events, NO volunteers.

Great beer deserves to be paired with great food! Savory eats will be available for purchase from some of Syracuse’ best food vendors.

BACK BY POPULAR DEMAND! Upgrade to VIP for an exclusive NY Beer & BBQ Pairing at Middle Ages Brewing, taking place before the festival at 2:30 PM. This one-of-a-kind experience features a curated flight of New York craft beers each paired with a BBQ dish by the famed Dinosaur BBQ.

VIP ticket holders will also receive special festival glassware, VIP swag, and access to exclusive VIP-only brews at the fest. Don’t wait – only 80 spots available!

With over a decade of experience, New York State Craft Brewers Festivals are produced with highest level of care and professionalism, with the goal of providing a truly authentic craft beer experience for all.

event.title: Sound of Music
event.description:
Tickets will go on sale to the general public on Oct 5th

For 65 years, THE SOUND OF MUSIC has been one of our “favorite things.” With its timeless story and irresistibly charming score, this Rodgers & Hammerstein classic isn’t just meant to be enjoyed – it’s meant to be shared. Now, a critically acclaimed North American tour brings the cherished musical to stages across the country to teach a new generation to sing.

Directed by three-time Tony Award® winner Jack O’Brien (Hairspray), this vibrant and romantic tale of Maria and the von Trapp family will captivate audiences with its universal themes of love, resilience and the power of music.

Featuring beloved songs like “Do-Re-Mi,” “Sixteen Going on Seventeen” and “Edelweiss,” THE SOUND OF MUSIC is the iconic tale of a spirited nun who chooses not to live behind closed doors – and, by following her heart, learns to climb every mountain.

THE SOUND OF MUSIC features music by Richard Rodgers, lyrics by Oscar Hammerstein II, and book by Howard Lindsay and Russel Crouse, suggested by The Trapp Family Singers by Maria Augusta Trapp. The 1965 Oscar®-winning film recently celebrated its 60th anniversary and continues to be one of the most successful movie musicals of all time.

www.SoundOfMusicOnTour.com

*Interpreters will be available at this performance

**Anyone, regardless of age, must have their own ticket.

event.title: Joe Bonamassa
event.description: Joe Bonamassa is one of today’s top live performers. His enthusiastic shows are one of the biggest parts of his career, and a favorite for music lovers worldwide. Hailed internationally as one of the greatest guitar players of his generation and cited by Guitar World Magazine as “the world’s biggest blues guitarist,” Bonamassa has almost single-handedly redefined the blues-rock genre and brought it into the mainstream. Backed by a stellar band of legendary musicians, the set list for this show will feature new songs alongside career-spanning favorites. By exceeding his own vertiginously high artistic goals, Bonamassa has shattered all expectations with 31 #1 Billboard Blues Albums (more than any other artist in history). Bonamassa’s career in the music industry has built steadily over the years and is only gaining more momentum.

event.title: Sonic Live In Concert
event.description:
Celebrate 35 years of one of the most iconic video game franchises of all time: Sonic the Hedgehog.  This new in concert experience brings together, live on stage, the most iconic music and incredible moments of the beloved Sonic video games. 

A live ensemble, rock musicians, electronics, and vocalists will perform an array of the incredible and defining songs from throughout the games as well as instrumental renditions of fan favourites from the Genesis era to now as they accompany the most exciting moments from across the games. From Green Hill Zone to “Undefeatable,” there’s no better way to celebrate Sonic’s rich history.

Audiences can expect musical Easter eggs woven into the arrangements and an electrifying production, adding an extra layer of discovery that brings Sonic’s world vividly to life on stage.

The concert also highlights the creative legacy behind Sonic’s music from legendary composers Jun Senoue and Tomoya Ohtani, whose work has helped define Sonic’s sound across generations.

This is a must-see show for Sonic fans!

event.title: The Wiz
event.description:
Individual show tickets are not available for sale at this time. Season tickets are available for purchase now. More information at: BroadwayinSyracuse.com 

This production uses haze, smoke and flashing lights.

The Tony® Award-winning Best Musical that took the world by storm is back.

THE WIZ returns “home” to stages across America in an all-new tour, direct from Broadway.

The Baltimore Sun raves “Powerhouse performances. Stunning choreography. Visionary sets” and the Chicago Sun-Times proclaims THE WIZ is “An eye-popping and high-intensity revival!”

This groundbreaking twist on The Wizard of Oz changed the face of Broadway—from its iconic score packed with soul, gospel, rock, and 70s funk to its stirring tale of Dorothy’s journey to find her place in a contemporary world.

With direction by Schele Williams (The Notebook, revival of Disney’s Aida), choreography by JaQuel Knight (Beyoncé’s “Single Ladies,” Black Is King) and additional material by Tony-nominated and Emmy-nominated writer and TV host Amber Ruffin (The Amber Ruffin Show, Late Night with Seth Meyers), this dynamite infusion of ballet, jazz, and modern pop brings a whole new groove to easing on down the road. Everybody rejoice!

**Anyone, regardless of age, must have their own ticket.

event.title: The Outsiders
event.description:
Individual show tickets are not available for sale at this time. Season tickets are available for purchase now. More information at: BroadwayinSyracuse.com 

The Outsiders includes flashing lights, loud noises, smoking on stage, and haze.

Due to the special effects, drops of water, washable red liquid, and small rubber pieces from the stage floor may land in the pit seating area.

The winner of four 2024 Tony Awards®, including Best Musical, is THE OUTSIDERS.

Adapted from S.E. HINTON’s seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA’s iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) and Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, and arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, and direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, “THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation.”

In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of ‘outsiders’ battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self-discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging…and the realization that there is still “lots of good in the world.”

*Interpreters will be available at this performance

**Anyone, regardless of age, must have their own ticket.

Blue Cactus

Rooted in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, Blue Cactus got their start among the active honky-tonk circuit, developing an electrified twang that now branches out effortlessly into folk, alt-country, and psychedelic-tinged rock. Having released three records to critical acclaim, they have grown a cult following in the South and beyond, their introspective lyricism and blistering guitar techniques making the band potent in the studio and on stage. Their 2025 album Believer was hailed in Bandcamp’s Best New Country list and earned them slots on SXSW, Hopscotch Fest’s main stage opening for Geese and My Morning Jacket, and PBS’ new original series, Shaped By Sound. Blue Cactus have toured throughout the US, developing a dedicated cult following. From intimate clubs to major festival stages, Blue Cactus is known for connecting deeply with audiences wherever they go.

linktr.ee/bluecactus

 

Ramona & the Holy Smokes

Formed in 2022, Ramona and the Holy Smokes have seen their star rise in the region and beyond. The band–which includes Kyle Kilduff (electric guitar), Brooks Hefner (pedal steel), Jay Ouypron (bass), and Porter Bralley (drums)–had built a rapport playing together before joining Ramona, and in their time together have brought their talents to Ramona’s songs and song ideas, shaping and arranging these for a signature honky tonk sound. The band has performed regularly in the region, appearing at several Americana festivals including Red Wing Roots (2024), Rooster Walk (2025), and Bristol Rhythm & Roots (2025), and has opened for touring artists like Margo Cilker, Colby Acuff, Willi Carlisle, Redd Volkaert, Joshua Hedley, Donna the Buffalo, and Kashus Culpepper.

linktr.ee/ramonaandtheholysmokes

 

Anna Kimm

Anna Kimm is a Charlotte-based singer-songwriter blending heartfelt storytelling with a hint of warm, melodic country charm. Her music pairs honest lyrics with dreamy Americana textures and a soulful edge. As she steps into a new era, Anna is evolving her sound into a more crossover country style, weaving together classic country roots, indie influences, and polished pop sensibilities to create something both timeless and fresh.

https://linktr.ee/annaxxkimm

event.title: MHS Annual Fundraiser Breakfast – October 1, 2026
event.description:
JOIN US FOR OUR ANNUAL FUNDRAISER BREAKFAST
Preserving our Past, Funding our Future

 
Date:  October 1, 2026
Location:  Trinity Presbyterian Church Fellowship Hall, 3115 Providence Road, Charlotte
Event Start: 8:30am

New this Year – 50/50 RAFFLE!
Feeling lucky? Join in our 50/50 raffle at the MHS Fundraiser Breakfast!
Half of the proceeds will support MHS, and one lucky winner will take home the other half.
Raffle tickets will be available for purchase at the event. Be sure to bring cash or check to participate! The lucky winner will be drawn during the breakfast. Thank you!

 

The Mecklenburg Historical Society will be holding its annual fundraising breakfast on Thursday, October 1, 2026 at Trinity Presbyterian Church at 3115 Providence Road, Charlotte, NC at 8:30am.

This year’s event will primarily support one of our most important sites, the Sugaw Creek Presbyterian Church and the historic cemeteries One and Two.  Cemetery Number One is one of the oldest city cemeteries in the country.  The church is the oldest in Mecklenburg County.

 
The Mecklenburg Historical Society has a team working at the church addressing the needs of the historic initiative.  Your support helps fund the above items.

The program will feature an engaging panel discussion on the progress and planned work.

 
Please click here to view the event flyer for details or to share with others.

October 2 at Hofbräuhaus Buffalo. Prost!

Whether you’re heading to the arena or just looking for the place to pregame, your Sabres game night starts at Hofbräuhaus Buffalo.

🏒 Pregame begins 2.5 hours before every home game.

event.title: 🏒🍺 EVERY SABRES HOME GAME STARTS AT OUR HAUS!
event.description:
🏒🍺 EVERY SABRES HOME GAME STARTS AT OUR HAUS!

Before the puck drops downtown, Pregame at Our Haus! Join us before every Buffalo Sabres home game for bier, food, games and a packed Haus full of Buffalo hockey fans.

The pregame starts 2.5 HOURS BEFORE PUCK DROP with:

🍺 Drink Specials
🍽️ Power Play Menu will get you in and out before the game!
💪 Stein Holding Competition one hour before puck drop with a chance to win a gift card for your next visit!

And on select home game nights marked with an *, we’re turning up the Bavarian atmosphere with LIVE GERMAN MUSIC! 🇩🇪🎶

Check out the schedule whether you will be pregaming with a DJ or German Band!

Regardless we’ve got music, bier, great food and a Haus full of Sabres fans getting ready for the game.

Whether you’re heading to the arena or just looking for the place to pregame, your Sabres game night starts at Hofbräuhaus Buffalo.

🏒 Pregame begins 2.5 hours before every home game.

PROST! 🍻 LET’S GO BUFFALO! 💙💛

event.title: Live German Music with our HAUS RESIDENCY!
event.description:
🇩🇪🍺 PROST! THE HAUS RESIDENCY IS HERE!

Nothing sounds quite like Hofbräuhaus Buffalo with live German music filling the Haus!

Our Haus Residency brings authentic Bavarian energy to the stage with rotating 2-piece and 3-piece performances featuring accordion, clarinet and all the German favorites that keep the bier flowing, the hands clapping and the whole Haus singing along. 🎶

Raise your liter, join in on a PROST and experience Hofbräuhaus the way it was meant to be experienced.

🪗 Live German Music
🍺 Fresh Hofbräu Bier
🥨 Authentic German Food
🇩🇪 Plenty of Bavarian fun

Bring your friends, grab a table and get ready to PROST! 🍻

Reserve your table on Resy.

event.title: Cock Robin LIVE at our HAUS! (NO GERMAN MUSIC)
event.description:
🎸 A legendary name in Buffalo rock returns to the stage!

Cock Robin helped define Western New York’s live music scene during the golden era of the 1970s, packing clubs from Buffalo to Syracuse and Cleveland with powerful vocals, outstanding musicianship and the kind of rock-and-roll energy that kept crowds partying until the music stopped.

Now, the legacy continues at Hofbräuhaus Buffalo!

📅 November 7
⏰ 7 to 10 PM
🎟️ $10 entertainment charge

Relive the music, the memories and the sound of one of Buffalo’s most beloved rock bands. Grab your friends, order a liter and prepare for a night of classic rock inside the Bierhall!

*THERE WILL NOT BE ANY GERMAN MUSIC TODAY

Reservations are strongly encouraged on Resy.

Classic rock, 2000s favorites, today’s hits and brunch at the Haus. Sounds like a pretty solid Sunday to us.

🍺 Hofbräu Bier

Grab your crew, order a liter and spend Sunday brunch with us!

event.title: 🏒🍺 EVERY SABRES HOME GAME STARTS AT OUR HAUS!
event.description:
🏒🍺 EVERY SABRES HOME GAME STARTS AT OUR HAUS!

Before the puck drops downtown, Pregame at Our Haus! Join us before every Buffalo Sabres home game for bier, food, games and a packed Haus full of Buffalo hockey fans.

The pregame starts 2.5 HOURS BEFORE PUCK DROP with:

🍺 Drink Specials
🍽️ Power Play Menu will get you in and out before the game!
💪 Stein Holding Competition one hour before puck drop with a chance to win a gift card for your next visit!

And on select home game nights marked with an *, we’re turning up the Bavarian atmosphere with LIVE GERMAN MUSIC! 🇩🇪🎶

Check out the schedule whether you will be pregaming with a DJ or German Band!

Regardless we’ve got music, bier, great food and a Haus full of Sabres fans getting ready for the game.

Whether you’re heading to the arena or just looking for the place to pregame, your Sabres game night starts at Hofbräuhaus Buffalo.

🏒 Pregame begins 2.5 hours before every home game.

PROST! 🍻 LET’S GO BUFFALO! 💙💛

🇩🇪🍺 PROST! THE HAUS RESIDENCY IS HERE!

Nothing sounds quite like Hofbräuhaus Buffalo with live German music filling the Haus!

🥨 Authentic German Food

Bring your friends, grab a table and get ready to PROST! 🍻

event.title: 🎻🎄 HOLIDAY STRINGS AT SUNDAY BRUNCH!
event.description:
🎻🎄 HOLIDAY STRINGS AT SUNDAY BRUNCH!

A little Christmas music, a cozy Sunday brunch and a beautiful way to celebrate the season. ❤️

Join us for Holiday Strings with Orchesterlehrern, a group of talented local orchestra teachers performing light classical music and holiday favorites live during brunch.

Expect familiar Christmas melodies, beautiful strings and all the warm, festive atmosphere of the holidays at the Haus.

🎻 Holiday Strings with Orchesterlehrern
🎄 Light Classical + Holiday Favorites
🍳 Sunday Brunch
📅 December 20 | 11AM–1PM

Bring the family, enjoy brunch and spend a festive Sunday morning surrounded by the sounds of the season. ✨

#HofbrauhausBuffalo #HolidayStrings #BuffaloBrunch #ChristmasInBuffalo #LiveMusicBuffalo #SundayBrunch

event.title: Christkindlmarkt 2026!
event.description:
🎄 The Christkindlmarkt countdown has begun!

Five festive weekends. One holiday tradition you won’t want to miss. Christkindlmarkt returns to Hofbräuhaus Buffalo November 20 through December 20, bringing the spirit of a traditional German Christmas market to our Haus! ✨

Make a little room in your holiday calendar for Christmas shopping, German food, a bier with friends, and time together. Whether it’s your first visit or an annual tradition, we can’t wait to celebrate the season with you!

🎁 Save these market dates:
November 20–22
November 27–29
December 4–6
December 10–13
December 18–20

Make a day of it and reserve a table for your meal on Resy. Christmas starts at our Haus! 🍻

event.title: 🏒🍺 EVERY SABRES HOME GAME STARTS AT OUR HAUS!
event.description:
🏒🍺 EVERY SABRES HOME GAME STARTS AT OUR HAUS!

Before the puck drops downtown, Pregame at Our Haus! Join us before every Buffalo Sabres home game for bier, food, games and a packed Haus full of Buffalo hockey fans.

The pregame starts 2.5 HOURS BEFORE PUCK DROP with:

🍺 Drink Specials
🍽️ Power Play Menu will get you in and out before the game!
💪 Stein Holding Competition one hour before puck drop with a chance to win a gift card for your next visit!

And on select home game nights marked with an *, we’re turning up the Bavarian atmosphere with LIVE GERMAN MUSIC! 🇩🇪🎶

Check out the schedule whether you will be pregaming with a DJ or German Band!

Regardless we’ve got music, bier, great food and a Haus full of Sabres fans getting ready for the game.

Whether you’re heading to the arena or just looking for the place to pregame, your Sabres game night starts at Hofbräuhaus Buffalo.

🏒 Pregame begins 2.5 hours before every home game.

PROST! 🍻 LET’S GO BUFFALO! 💙💛

event.title: Live German Music with our HAUS RESIDENCY!
event.description:
🇩🇪🍺 PROST! THE HAUS RESIDENCY IS HERE!

Nothing sounds quite like Hofbräuhaus Buffalo with live German music filling the Haus!

Our Haus Residency brings authentic Bavarian energy to the stage with rotating 2-piece and 3-piece performances featuring accordion, clarinet and all the German favorites that keep the bier flowing, the hands clapping and the whole Haus singing along. 🎶

Raise your liter, join in on a PROST and experience Hofbräuhaus the way it was meant to be experienced.

🪗 Live German Music
🍺 Fresh Hofbräu Bier
🥨 Authentic German Food
🇩🇪 Plenty of Bavarian fun

Bring your friends, grab a table and get ready to PROST! 🍻

Reserve your table on Resy.

event.title: Midnight in Munich 2027! Ring in 2027 Just Like We Are in Bavaria!
event.description:
🍾🇩🇪 MIDNIGHT IN MUNICH 2027! 🇩🇪🍾

Why wait until midnight when we can celebrate New Year’s Eve Munich-style?!

We’re ringing in 2027 when the clock strikes midnight in Munich, which means the celebration starts EARLY at Hofbräuhaus Buffalo!

Join us for an afternoon of live German music with Die Haus Band, Hofbräu bier, German food and plenty of PROSTING as we count down to the New Year right along with Munich. 🍺🎶

🎉 Midnight in Munich 2027
🪗 Live with Die Haus Band
🕓 December 31 | 4PM–7PM
🍺 Hofbräu Bier
🥨 Authentic German Food
🇩🇪 A Munich-style New Year’s celebration

Bring the whole family, raise a liter and celebrate 2027 the Bavarian way!

PROST TO THE NEW YEAR! 🍻🎆

Reservations recommended at hofbrauhausbuffalo.com.

#HofbrauhausBuffalo #MidnightInMunich #NewYearsEve #BuffaloNYE #LiveGermanMusic #Prost #BuffaloNY

event.title: 2026 Belle Meade Society Fall Dinner
event.description:
The Greensboro History Museum’s Belle Meade Society will have its annual Fall Dinner at the museum on Monday, October 5, 2026. The evening starts at 5:30 pm and includes dinner, wine and a presentation by Kevin von der Lippe.

Drawing from the research conducted for the book Greensboro Depot, local railroad enthusiast von der Lippe will discuss how photographs, newspapers, maps, railroad records, and materials from private collections were assembled to document the history of one of Greensboro’s best-known landmarks. The presentation will feature images from the book as well as several photographs that did not appear in the final publication, providing a behind-the-scenes look at the sources and methods used to preserve and share local history.

$45 per person. Please RSVP by Friday, September 25.

Purchase Your Tickets Online

It isn’t too late to become a Belle Meade member, by upgrading your current membership or joining anew. We hope to see you!

event.title: Richard Kurin, History by a Hair: Thomas Jefferson, Sally Hemings & Solving a 200-Year-Old Mystery
event.description:
The Smithsonian Institution’s Distinguished Scholar and Ambassador-at-Large Richard Kurin discusses his new book.

History by a Hair is the definitive account of how a discarded strand of hair found in Thomas Jefferson’s Bible at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History led to a sweeping, multi-year genomic investigation, drawing on technological advances in DNA to finally resolve a 200-year national controversy.

Book signing to follow with copies available to purchase from Scuppernong Books.

Spaces are limited. Let us know you are attending. 

About the author
Richard Kurin is the Smithsonian Institution’s Distinguished Scholar and Ambassador-at-Large and previously served as Under Secretary overseeing all museums and scientific centers. An author of several popular books on American history and Fellow of the American Academy of Arts & Sciences, Kurin has led major national cultural initiatives and produced award-winning public history.

This event is part of the Greensboro History Museum’s America250 community programming. As the country marks its 250th anniversary, the museum invites residents to have fun exploring the past, reflect on our shared history and be part of a picture of our city today. event.title: Revolutionary Road Trip: A Conversation with Darley Newman
event.description:
Travel expert Darley Newman chats with Museum Director Carol Ghiorsi Hart about her new book, Revolutionary Road Trip: Hidden Stories of America’s Founding Journey. The book follows the host of PBS’s Travels with Darley on a journey through American Revolution sites, including right here in Guilford County.

Seats are limited. Registration for this event is coming soon. Check back for more information.

About the author

Darley Newman is an award-winning host, producer, author, and travel expert recognized by Forbes for building a “PBS media empire.” She’s blended world-record feats with purposeful storytelling—from leaping off the world’s highest commercial bungee in Macao to riding horses across Botswana to interviewing civil rights witnesses and small business owners in rural United States. As the creator and host of Travels with Darley, Equitrekking, and Look Up with Darley, she combines travel, history, and narrative to uncover hidden gems across the United States and around the world. A trusted, authentic voice, her series and podcast reach dedicated fans on PBS, Amazon Prime, iHeart, and internationally in more than eighty-five nations. Darley has earned multiple Emmy Award nominations for hosting, writing, producing, and directing. She’s been honored with the North American Travel Journalist Award, Inspiring Woman Award, two Telly Awards, and induction into the Taste Awards Hall of Fame. Having filmed her series in destinations as close to home as New York City and Los Angeles and as far afield as Seoul, Uruguay, and Dubai, she inspires audiences to explore beyond their comfort zones. She is a graduate of The George Washington University.

Yevgeny Kutik, violin

With a “dark-hued tone and razor-sharp technique” (The New York Times), violinist Yevgeny Kutik has captivated audiences worldwide with an old-world sound that communicates a modern intellect. Praised for his technical precision and virtuosity, he is lauded for his poetic and imaginative interpretations of standard works as well as rarely heard and newly composed repertoire.

A native of Minsk, Belarus, Yevgeny Kutik immigrated to the United States with his family at the age of five. His 2014 album, Music from the Suitcase: A Collection of Russian Miniatures (Marquis Classics), features music he found in his family’s suitcase after immigrating to the United States from the Soviet Union in 1990 and debuted at No. 5 on the Billboard Classical chart. The album garnered critical acclaim and was featured on NPR’s All Things Considered and in The New York Times.

Committed to the music of our time, Kutik regularly gives premiere and repeat performances of major works by today’s most celebrated composers, and performs with leading orchestras across the country. In recent seasons, he has given the world premiere of Cântico, a work for solo violin by Andreia Pinto Correia co-commissioned for him by the Boston Symphony Orchestra and made his debut with the Detroit Symphony Orchestra led by Leonard Slatkin, performing the world premiere of Joseph Schwantner’s Violin Concerto, written specifically for him. Other rRecent and upcoming highlights include a solo performance with the Louisville Orchestra conducted by Ziwei Ma; the world premiere performance of a new violin concerto written by Eric Nathan with the Rhode Island Philharmonic, led by Ruth Reinhardt; plus solo performances with the Phoenix Symphony under Andrew Litton; and the Grant Park Music Festival under Leonard Slatkin. Kutik makes his Wisconsin Philharmonic debut this season, performing Tchaikovsky’s Violin Concerto in D Major, led by Alexander Platt. With conductor Michelle Merrill, Kutik will perform Philip Glass’s Violin Concerto No. 2 “The American Four Seasons” as soloist with the Winston-Salem Symphony and The Coastal Symphony of Georgia, having performed the concerto last season with Merrill and the Las Vegas Philharmonic. He recently gave the world premiere of Scattered Light by Jonathan Leshnoff presented by Newport Classical. Currently, Andrea Casarrubios is working on a new recital work composed for him.  

Performance highlights for Kutik include his debuts at the Kennedy Center presented by Washington Performing Arts, and at the Ravinia Festival. He has appeared in recital as a part of the Dame Myra Hess Concerts Chicago; at UCLA; Peoples’ Symphony Concerts, Kaufman Music Center, and National Sawdust in New York City; the Embassy Series and The Phillips Collection in Washington D.C.; and at the Lobkowicz Collections Prague presented by Prince William Lobkowicz. Festival performances have included the Tanglewood Music Festival, Cape Cod Chamber Music Festival, Ravinia, the Ludwigsburger Schlossfestspiele in Germany, and the Verbier Festival in Switzerland.     

Kutik made his major orchestral debut in 2003 with Keith Lockhart and The Boston Pops as the First Prize recipient of the Boston Symphony Orchestra Young Artists Competition, and has since performed with orchestras throughout the country including the Rochester and Dayton Philharmonics; Detroit, Tallahassee, New Haven, Asheville, Wyoming, La Crosse and Glacier symphony orchestras; as well as Florida’s SYMPHONIA, New York City’s Riverside Symphony and Park Avenue Chamber Symphony, the Pro Arte Chamber Orchestra of Boston. Abroad, he has appeared as guest soloist with Germany’s Norddeutsche Philharmonie Rostock and WDR Rundfunk Orchestra Köln, Montenegro’s Montenegrin Symphony Orchestra, Japan’s Tokyo Vivaldi Ensemble, and the Cape Town Philharmonic in South Africa.  

Kutik’s additional releases on Marquis include The Death of Juliet and Other Tales (2021), which highlights folklore and folktales portrayed in the music of Prokofiev. The album features new arrangements by Kutik, Michael Gandolfi, and Kati Agócs, commissioned specifically for the album. In 2019, he released Meditations on Family, for which he commissioned eight composers to translate a personal family photo into a short musical miniature for violin and various ensemble, envisioning the project as a living archive of new works inspired by memories, home, and belonging. Strings Magazine featured Kutik as its cover story for the March/April issue, reporting, “True to Kutik’s vision, each miniature is a window into the composer’s emotional life.” Featured composers include Joseph Schwantner, Andreia Pinto Correia, Gity Razaz, Timo Andres, Chris Cerrone, Kinan Azmeh, Gregory Vajda, and Paola Prestini. Kutik’s 2016 album, Words Fail, uses Mendelssohn’s Songs Without Words as a starting point to expand upon the idea that music surpasses traditional language in its expressive capabilities. His 2012 debut album, Sounds of Defiance, features the music of Achron, Pärt, Schnittke, and Shostakovich, focusing on music written during the darkest periods of the lives of these composers. Kutik also recorded episode six of Gerard Schwarz’s All-Star Orchestra, a made-for-television classical music concert series released on DVD by Naxos and broadcast nationally on PBS, performing Joseph Schwantner’s The Poet’s Hour – Soliloquy for Violin.    

Passionate about his heritage and its influence on his artistry, Kutik remains closely involved with the organizations that helped bring his family to the United States. He regularly speaks and performs across the country to raise awareness and support for refugees from around the world. He was a featured performer at the 2012 March of the Living observances, playing at the Krakow Opera House and for more than 20,000 people at Auschwitz-Birkenau.

Yevgeny Kutik began violin studies with his mother, Alla Zernitskaya, and went on to study with Zinaida Gilels, Shirley Givens, Roman Totenberg, and Donald Weilerstein. He holds a bachelor’s degree from Boston University and a master’s degree from the New England Conservatory and currently resides in Boston. Kutik is ​​the Artistic Director and co-founder of The Birch Festival, built around connecting and integrating leading musicians with the Berkshire community, while highlighting the unique and original stories of those who make up the Berkshires. He is the recipient of the Salon de Virtuosi Grant as well as the Tanglewood Music Center Jules Reiner Violin Prize. Yevgeny performs on an 1850 J.B. Vuillaume violin made in Paris. For more information, please visit www.yevgenykutik.com.

Michelle Merrill, conductor

WSS Music Director Michelle Merrill served four years as the Assistant and then Associate Conductor of the Detroit Symphony Orchestra and also serves as the Music Director of the Coastal Symphony of Georgia, where she has ignited the growth and expansion of the orchestra’s offerings both on and off the stage.  Ms. Merrill is a proud recipient of a 2016 Solti Foundation U.S. Career Assistance Award as well as the prestigious 2013 Ansbacher Conducting Fellowship as awarded by members of the Vienna Philharmonic and the American Austrian Foundation, which enabled her to be in residence at the world-renowned Salzburg Festival.

Vuillaume violin made in Paris. For more information, please visit www.yevgenykutik.com.

event.excerpt: Hear two Winston-Salem Symphony premieres on one concert! Enjoy the Symphony’s first-ever performance of the overture to Beethoven’s only ballet, Creatures of Prometheus, plus the vibrant violinist Yevgeny Kutik in the Second Violin Concerto of Philip Glass. Known for his mesmerizing “minimalist” sound, Glass’s music has a broad appeal among symphony audiences, opera lovers, and movie buffs. Brahms’ captivating First Symphony—which took Brahms over twenty years to write—balances the program.

BPRD program participants should attend clinic at the high school they will go to (per Bismarck Public Schools feeder system).

  • Bismarck High School, 800 N. 8th St. – Enter the doors in the parking lot loop and in the Karlgaard main gym.
  • Legacy High School, 3400 E. Calgary Ave. – Enter main door #1.

Registration

Attendance is FREE and all BPRD registered participants are encouraged to attend.

event.title: Night Watchman Evening Tours
event.description:
|

Join Old Salem’s night watchmen on their lantern-lit nightly rounds as we investigate true stories from the records…stories of spirits and fires, of ruffians and corpses!

Experience the original building where these mysteries and tragedies took place, and step into a time of instability and many unknowns. Learn about Salem’s most famous legend, as well as stories you have never heard before. How did the early inhabitants of Salem grapple with the dangers and suspense of their world, and make sense of supernatural phenomena?

Grab a cloak and lantern, and join the night watch to see for yourself!

This exciting tour is our most in-depth yet, and is designed for suspense-seeking guests ages 10+. This is a partially outdoor walking tour, on uneven streets, and in buildings with stairs. The tour may be held regardless of weather conditions.

Six tours will be held nightly, beginning at 6:30 PM with the final tour beginning at 7:45 PM. The tour is approximately 60 minutes in length, and 12 tickets are available for each time slot.

event.description:
|

American colonists and Americans in the new republic experienced one constant: change. From changing political identities, geographic boundaries, and conceptions of freedom, American lives constantly evolved. This seminar will explore the ways that craftspeople and cabinetmakers navigated this ever-shifting political and social landscape and the ways that they reflected shifting American and European tastes and identities in their work.

You can join us in Winston-Salem or online for this two day seminar. Participants will engage in two days of lectures, including a keynote address by Dr. Tiffany Momon, Director of the Center for Historic Preservation, Middle Tennessee State University and Founder of the Black Craftspeople Digital Archive, as well as opportunities to participate in pre-conference workshops and a furniture open house in MESDA’s study galleries.

event.description:
|

Learn how southern women exercised power in the early American South.

At 2:00 PM, join us to learn about the Edenton Tea Party, one of the first organized women’s political protests in America. On October 25, 1774, a group of Edenton women led by Penelope (Padgett) Barker (1728-1796) pledged to boycott imported British tea and cloth in response to the Tea Act of 1774. News of their “tea party” reached London, where it was reported in the Morning Chronicle and London Advertiser on January 16, 1775.

These guided tours are included with your standard admission.

FREE fun for the whole family! Explore the Museum together and engage with the exhibitions and art making in new and exciting ways. Project Announcement & Registration begin the month before each event.

Printober is back! Join us during the Fargo Studio Crawl for the return of this favorite annual printmaking event. Try your hand at screen printing and print one of this year’s featured designs onto a T-shirt, tote bag, or another flat fabric item you bring from home. We’ll provide the ink, screens, and instruction- just bring something to print on and enjoy a fun, creative activity for all ages!

Community Engagement programs are made possible with funding from Xcel Energy Foundation, Alex Stern Family Foundation, Otter Tail Corporation Foundation, and Kiwanis Club of Fargo.

event.description: We embrace the unique qualities of all who walk through our doors and appreciate that many visitors need to explore the Museum in different ways. event.title: FestiBull of Lights
event.description:
[vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text css=”” bottom_margin=”20px”]FestiBull of Lights transforms the Durham Bulls Athletic Park into a dazzling winter wonderland! Stroll through thousands of twinkling lights synchronized to festive music, creating a magical holiday experience for all ages. Meet Santa, hop aboard the NC by Train Holiday Express, create seasonal crafts, roast s’mores, savor festive food and drinks, and enjoy even more holiday fun — all surrounded by a breathtaking display of lights![/vc_column_text]Get Tickets [vc_column_text css=”” bottom_margin=”40px”]

Dates & Times

Open: November 19 – January 2 (closed on November 26, November 30, December 7, December 14. December 25)
Time: 5:30-9:00pm every night[/vc_column_text]

[vc_column_text css=”” bottom_margin=”40px”]

Attractions

[/vc_column_text]

NC by Train Holiday Express

All aboard! Ride the NC by Train Holiday Express around the field for unbeatable views of the lights. Seating is limited nightly — pre-purchase your ticket add-on to guarantee a spot!

Meet Santa & Wool E. Claus

Visit Santa nightly to share your wish list and snap a photo in his sleigh before he returns to the North Pole on Christmas Eve! Wool E. Claus will be spreading cheer every night, too.

Holiday Craft Zone

Stop by Santa’s Workshop to create free holiday crafts — fun for kids of all ages, every night!

Scavenger Hunt

Put your detective skills to the test! Complete the holiday scavenger hunt and return your list to win a prize.

Letters to Santa

Write your letter to Santa and hand-deliver it during your visit — or drop it in our special mailbox for express delivery to the North Pole!

Christmas Tree Alley

Wander through a forest of uniquely decorated Christmas trees — each one full of festive flair and holiday magic.

S’mores & Firepits

Warm up by the fire and roast marshmallows with friends and family. S’mores kits are available for purchase on-site.

Holiday Slide

Experience the excitement of our Holiday Slide! This snow-free thrill ride is perfect for all ages — don’t miss your chance to zoom down!

Heated Holiday Lounge

Step inside the Heated Holiday Lounge to escape the winter chill! Relax in our cozy space before heading back out to experience more holiday magic.

Jingle Bell Dance Floor

Step onto the Jingle Bell Dance Floor and dance beneath a dazzling display of colorful disco lights! It’s a magical experience that’s fun for kids and guests of all ages.

[vc_column_text css=”” bottom_margin=”40px”]

Tickets

General Admission

$12 / person in advance, $13/ person on event day. Limited tickets available nightly. Purchase online in advance or at the Bulls Box Office (Mon–Fri, 9AM–5PM) or call (919) 687-6500. Tickets required for all guests 3 and up. Get Tickets

Flex Ticket Add-On

$3/person – By purchasing a flex ticket add-on, you have the ability to exchange your ticket to a different night if something comes up! Just contact the ticket office at (919) 687-6500 before the gates open on the day you purchased and you can move your ticket to a new date! Get Tickets

Train Ticket Add-On

$5/person – Reserve your spot on the NC by Train Holiday Express. Train tickets are limited nightly and are sold only as an add-on to the general admission ticket. Ticket is good for one ride on the train for the night purchased. Get Tickets

Show your NC by Train ticket at the Durham Bulls Box Office on the day you are attending FestiBull of Lights to receive a free NC by Train Holiday Express ticket!

Private Firepits

$200 for up to 8 people – Enjoy your own private firepit for the entire night while taking in the magic of FestiBull of Lights. Includes a s’mores kit for 8, perfect for roasting marshmallows and creating cozy holiday memories together. Get Tickets

Exclusive Igloos

$400 for 8 people – Create lasting memories in one of our cozy private igloos, offering a unique and intimate way to experience the magic of FestiBull of Lights. Igloo includes admission, one train ride per person, an unlimited hot chocolate bar, cookie platter, and s’mores kit with private fire pit. Get Tickets [/vc_column_text]

[vc_column_text css=”” bottom_margin=”40px”]

Large Groups

Gather your coworkers, friends, family, school, or community group for a memorable holiday outing at FestiBull of Lights! Whether you’re looking to reserve a private area of the stadium or bring a group of guests to enjoy the lights together, we offer flexible group experiences to fit your needs. To plan your group visit, email groups@durhambulls.com or call 919-687-6500.

Luxury Suites

Celebrate the season in your own private, climate-controlled Luxury Suite, the perfect setting for holiday parties, family gatherings, and client entertainment while enjoying the magic of FestiBull of Lights. Catering is available for an additional cost.

Sugar Plum Suite (CBC Suite): $45 per person, minimum 25 people, max 40 people
Snowflake Suite (Suite 8): $35 per person, minimum 20 people, max 30 people

PNC Triangle Club

Perched atop Durham Bulls Athletic Park, the PNC Triangle Club offers a premium indoor holiday experience with stunning panoramic views of the stadium and FestiBull of Lights. This elevated event space provides a warm, festive atmosphere perfect for groups of 50–250, creating an unforgettable setting for holiday gatherings, celebrations, and special events.[/vc_column_text]

[vc_column_text css=”” bottom_margin=”20px”]

Frequently Asked Questions

[/vc_column_text]

What are the event hours?

FestiBull of Lights is open nightly from 5:30 PM to 9:00 PM. The last entry into the park is at 8:30 PM.

What does my ticket include?

All tickets are general admission and include access to all free attractions, such as – Holiday Craft Zone, Photos with Santa & Wool E. Claus, Scavenger Hunt, Letters to Santa, Christmas Tree Alley, Fire Pits, Holiday Slide, Heated Holiday Lounge, and the Jingle Bell Dance Floor.

How can I purchase tickets?

We recommend buying tickets in advance online. You can also purchase them in person at the Bulls Box Office (Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM) or by phone at 919-687-6500.

Do children need a ticket?

Children 2 years old and under are admitted free and do not require a ticket.

What is the cancellation policy?

If the event is officially canceled due to weather, you will receive an email with instructions on how to exchange your ticket for another available 2026 FestiBull of Lights date (subject to availability). Refunds are not available. To reschedule, bring your original ticket to the Bulls Box Office or call us at 919-687-6500.

Is there a clear bag policy?

Bags or containers larger than 16″ x 16″ x 8″ are not allowed inside Durham Bulls Athletic Park. Bags within the allowed size do not need to be clear, but all bags are subject to search. Diaper bags and medical bags larger than the limit are permitted. Click here for a full list of prohibited items.

How does my company get involved?

To learn more about how your company can get involved with this year’s event email sponsorship@durhambulls.com.

event.title: Mahjong Social Club
event.description:
Looking for your new favorite weekly tradition? Join Mahjong Social Club, a five-week Mahjong series hosted by Rhinegeist in partnership with Cincy Shuffle! Whether you’re learning the game for the first time or looking for a welcoming place to play, this series is designed for all skill levels.


Wednesdays | September 9 – October 7

6:00 PM – 8:30 PM

Rhinegeist Private Events – Signature Room + Lounge

The best part? Attend one session, a few, or all five! Each week is designed to be enjoyed on its own, making it easy to fit Mahjong into your schedule while building your skills at your own pace.

Each week, choose the experience that’s right for you:

Beginner Lessons (Lounge) $60

New to Mahjong or need a refresher? Learn the fundamentals in a fun, welcoming environment with experienced instructors from Cincy Shuffle. No experience needed!

Open Play (Signature Room) $20

Ready to play? Join our open Mahjong tables to practice your skills, meet fellow players, and enjoy friendly games with Cincinnati’s growing Mahjong community. To attend this session, you must know how to play and provide your own 2026 rule card.

Purchase your 2026 National Mahjong rule card here!

We’ve got you covered! All Mahjong tiles, racks, mats, and learning materials are provided by Cincy Shuffle, so all you need to do is show up ready to learn and play. To participate in the open play, don’t forget to provide your own rule card! Expect fun giveaways and prizes each night! Rhinegeist’s full selection of beer, cider, cocktails, wine, NA beverages, and soft drinks will be available for purchase throughout the evening.

Tickets

Make Mahjong Social Club your new Wednesday night tradition! Whether you’re bringing friends or coming solo, Mahjong Social Club is the perfect place to learn, play, connect, and unwind. Grab a drink, pull up a chair, and we’ll see you at the table!

Additional Information: 

All ages welcome. Space is limited, so advance registration is encouraged. Tickets are non-refundable. Rhinegeist reserves the right to refuse service to intoxicated guests.

event.title: Walking for A Second Look
event.description:
This two-hour walk will begin at the Over-the-Rhine Museum at 3 West McMicken Avenue to briefly discuss the exhibition, Second Look: Danny Ransohoff’s Cityscapes Through New Eyes. From there, with copies of Danny Ransohoff’s historic photos in hand, the group will walk to five of the locations featured in the show. Once oriented in each spot, we will discuss change over time by comparing the photograph of the past and present before our eyes. We may even begin to imagine the neighborhood’s future. This walk will be led by University of Cincinnati Research Assistant Professor of History, Anne Delano Steinert.

Additional Information: Participants should come dressed for the weather and expect moderate exercise. Please RSVP to hello@otrmuseum.org to stay informed in case of inclement weather.

event.title: Dayton Bus Tour
event.description:
Spotlight Weekends highlight FotoFocus Biennial Venues within specific geographic locations where artists and curators will be on site for talks, tours, special events, and featured programming. This is an opportunity to immerse yourself in the vibrant energy of the FotoFocus Biennial, exploring art within the communities that create and present it.

The Bus Tour is now full. To join the waitlist, please email pass@fotofocus.org.

8:00am Meet at FotoFocus Center / Ziegler Garage

8:30am Depart Cincinnati

10:00am Wright State University

Elizabeth Mead: Incident(als): objects + things, sculpture + photographs. Sculptural objects and images paired together to magnify the significance of seemingly small things and fleeting experiences.

Holly Roberts: Confluence. Hauntingly layered visual narratives experimenting with hybridity and transformation, where image and imagination converge. 

Tours given by professors and curators Stefan Chinov and Tracy Longley-Cook.

11:00am Sinclair Community College Art Galleries

Katria Foster: Domestic Affair. Highlights physical and mental aspects of the female perspective, ruminating on themes of control, manipulation, and unquestioned social constructs.

Emily Wiethorn: The Death of You and Me. Photographic series examining memory, suffering, and the life-altering effects of trauma.

Introduction with Galleries Coordinator, Amanda Darrah, followed by self-guided tour.

11:35pm Dayton Society of Artists

Luminous Flow. An open call positing long-exposure photography as a way to reveal motion, energy, and the passage of time through landscapes, cityscapes, and experimental processes. 

Short presentation of the exhibition provided by juror Gregory Changa Freeman.

-OR-

Stivers School for the Arts

Heather Wetzel: Considering the Cultivated. Interrogates the role humans have on the environment, ecosystems, and food production through historic photographic processes, paper making, book arts, and sculptural materials.

Gallery tour led by Leah Stahl, Director of Photography and Media Arts.

12:20pm Edward A. Dixon Gallery

Picturing Tomorrow: Speculative Futures in Lens-Based Art. Invites artists to consider how photography can be used to document not just what is, but also speculate on what could be.

Gallery tour led by owner and founder, Ed Dixon.

12:50pm Lunch

1:20pm Dayton Art Institute

Looking for Japan: Early Japanese Photography. Captures Japan’s Meiji period through postcards, albums, albumen travel photographs, and hanging scroll collotypes, reflecting on social transformation and Western influences. 

Getting Technical: Alternative Photographic Processes. A group exhibition spanning 175 years, embracing photography’s founding spirit of experimentation through uncommon techniques and adaptations.

Curator talk with Mariah Postlewait, Sara M. and Michelle Vance Waddell Curator of Feminist Art and Photography.

2:00pm The Contemporary Dayton 

Ella Kraimer: Appearances. Large-scale photographic self-portraits examining identity, performance, and consumption in a digital culture shaped by spectacle and self-surveillance. 

Stacy Kranitz: Ain’t No Grave Gonna Hold My Body Down. Documents how images and archives have shaped and distorted public understanding of Appalachia across generations.

Public artist talk featuring Stacy Kranitz in conversation with Andrew Milward, author and Director of Graduate Studies, Creative Writing Division, at the University of Kentucky. Interim Director and Chief Curator Heather Jones will also be on site.

3:45pm University of Dayton: Roger Glass Center for the Arts

Darshan. Collaborative documentary work of India exploring the Hindu philosophy and phenomenon of darshan (“to see”).

Gallery talk led by Nicholaus Arnold, Galleries Director.

5:00pm Rosewood Arts Center

Amanda Bradley: Notations from Home. Images exploring diasporic notions of home across geographies and time, using the camera as a tool for note-taking and relationship building.  

Trent Davis Bailey: The North Fork. Childhood memories intertwined with images and moments from family farms on Colorado’s Western Slope.

Gallery tour and artist talk led by Trent Davis Bailey. Laura Truitt, Gallery Coordinator, and Shayna McConville, Division Manager of Cultural Arts, will also be on site. Reception with light refreshments to follow. 

7:15pm Arrive in Cincinnati

event.title: Columbus Bus Tour
event.description:
Spotlight Weekends highlight FotoFocus Biennial Venues within specific geographic locations where artists and curators will be on site for talks, tours, special events, and featured programming. This is an opportunity to immerse yourself in the vibrant energy of the FotoFocus Biennial, exploring art within the communities that create and present it.

To RSVP, please email pass@fotofocus.org. Seating is limited. Biennial Pass required.

9:00am Meet at FotoFocus Center / Ziegler Garage

11:30am Wexner Center for the Arts

Sammy Baloji: When Extraction Becomes Form It Speaks In Borrowed Tongues. Uncovers how colonial extraction shaped the flow of people, materials, forms, and culture across Africa, Europe, and the Atlantic world through photography, film, and sculpture.

Gallery tour led by Sarah Robison, Curator of Teaching, Learning, and Interpretation, and Rebecca Lowery, Curator of Exhibitions. Interim Executive Director & Head of Advancement hope to join as well.

12:30pm Lunch in the Performance Space / Black Box

1:30pm Columbus Museum of Art

Queer Constellations: Photographs from the Aronowitz Family Collection. Traces artistic lineage and identity through photographs by and about queer artists, illustrating how photographers across generations shape histories and create visibility.

Gallery tour led by Kaitlin Booher, Associate Curator of Photography.

2:30pm Columbus College of Art & Design: Beeler Gallery

Haunting. Examines time as a haunting force, reaching across burial grounds, pandemics, atomic history, gun violence, and ecological loss to reveal what the visible image cannot hold.

Gallery tour led by new Executive Director Kyle Herrington and Registrar Melissa Vogley.

3:15pm Shot Tower Gallery

One Shot. Alumni exhibition highlighting the impact of the Photography Career Program at Fort Hayes, an incubator for emerging image-makers to explore photography as a form of artistic expression and storytelling.

Gallery tour led by Stephen Takacs, Career-Technical Education (CTE) Photography Instructor.

4:00pm ROY G BIV Gallery

Franklinton Across Time: The Floodplain Imagination. A living archive examining the history of one of Columbus’ oldest neighborhoods through contemporary lens-based work, archival materials, interviews, and site-responsive installations, reflecting on collective memory and urban change.

Gallery tour with Executive Gallery Director, Bethani Blake.

Reception & light bites.

5:00pm Depart ROY G BIV Gallery

7:00pm Arrive back in Cincinnati

event.title: Cincinnati Bus Tour
event.description:
Spotlight Weekends highlight FotoFocus Biennial Venues within specific geographic locations where artists and curators will be on site for talks, tours, special events, and featured programming. This is an opportunity to immerse yourself in the vibrant energy of the FotoFocus Biennial, exploring art within the communities that create and present it.

The Bus Tour is now full. To join the waitlist, please email pass@fotofocus.org.

8:30am Meet at FotoFocus Center / Ziegler Garage

9:00am Kennedy Heights Arts Center

Cultural Ties. Celebrates Latin American culture through photography, mixed media, and short films, offering a multi-sensory exploration of place, history, and identity.

Gallery tour led by Mallory Feltz, Director of Exhibitions and Public Art. Artists and film curator Mary Leonard will be in attendance and will discuss their work.

10:00am Eisele Gallery

Waiting to Be Seen. A selection of street photography and photojournalism paying tribute to the diversity of urban life and to the lens-based artists who witness and capture it.

Gallery tour led by Sandy Eichert, curator, and/or David Smith, gallery owner.

10:45am Cincinnati Art Club

Contemporary Tintype Portraits and Altered Historic Images. Tintype portraits by Ricky Willis Tintypes and Blue Creek Tinworks celebrating the local photographic community alongside altered historic images from the Cincinnati Art Club archives.

Curatorial overview provided by Kip Eagen. Artists/studios may also be present to speak about the process and history of tintype photography.

11:30am Lunch @ Swell Art Cafe

12:15pm Wave Pool

Forgetting is Everywhere. Work by four artists exploring transformations both slow and sudden, unexpected but also predestined. Presented in conjunction with Swell.

Gallery tour led by curator Calcagno Cullen.

1:00pm Studio Kroner

Erika NJ Allen: Beneath All Distance. Investigates deep time, material memory, and humanity’s relationship to landscapes shaped by endurance and change through analog photography and ceramics.

Open gallery roaming and artist talk with Erika NJ Allen. Paul Kroner will also be on site.

1:45pm Art Academy of Cincinnati

Depth of Field. An open call highlighting student artists considering the present state of photography and its possible future directions.

Noel Bassam Mohammad Maghathe: Over Everything. Examines how memory is shaped, altered, and reconstructed through the act of retrieval, initiating a dialogue between longing, connection, and memory.

Untwined/Interwoven. Reflects on concepts of place and time, examining the ephemeral, impermanent, and fragmented nature of photography.

Accra Shepp: Bearing Witness. Presents three bodies of work—Occupying Wall Street, The Covid Journals, and The Islands of New York—that delve into subjects often overlooked or intentionally misconstrued.

Gallery talks led by Michael Hurst, Director of Exhibitions; Rachel Reisert, Head of Photography; and student curators.

3:00pm Taft Museum of Art 

Edie McKee Harper: Modernist at Play. Over 100 works across a variety of media, including photography, demonstrate the artist’s distinctive modernist vision, highlighting her minimalist and often playful style.

Introduction by Curator Tamera Lenz Muente followed by a self-guided tour.

3:45pm Annex Gallery 

Juan-Sí González: I.T.I.N.E.R.A.T.I.O.N.S. Explores the boundary between documentary and fiction, reinterpreting reality as metaphor and calling attention to shared physical, ideological, and psychological landscapes.

Artist talk with Juan-Sí González. Jorge Rodríguez Diez, Executive Director and Chief Curator, and Jens Rosenkrantz may also be on site.

4:15pm Depart Annex Gallery. Bus returns to Ziegler Garage on Sycamore Street.

event.title: Architectures of Amnesia
event.description:
By reexamining Donald Judd’s time in occupied Korea, this talk uncovers how war, empire, and historical amnesia became embedded in postwar American art, including works in Natural Fictions.

Additional Information: This event will take place at Northern Kentucky University. Visit the Carnegie website for more details.

event.title: Distance of the Moon
event.description:
Weaving together personal memories, myths, scientific discoveries and speculative histories, Distance of the Moon is an expanded cinema performance that meditates on yearning and proposes strategies to reach unreachable places.

Additional Information: Gallery is wheelchair accessible.
